_passive_, **feast together**, {{NT+4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Eudemia” 1245b5, 2nd-1st c.BC: Posidonius Historicus 15J., 1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 2.355; ὑμῖν NT.2Pet.2.13, compare 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Antiquitates Judaicae” 1.3.5, “BGU” 596.10 (1st c.AD), 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “VH” 2.15, etc.}}; [ἀνδριάντι] {{Refs|“PMag.Par.” 1.3150.}}
4915:
Related to: ** ἡλῐκι-ώτης**, ου, ὁ,
Cretan dialect **ϝαλικιώτας** (written βαλικιώτης), {{Refs 5th c.AD+|5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus}}:— **equal in age, comrade**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.71, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 1006, 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.48; ἡ. τινί 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 20.36}}; ἐμὸς ἡ. {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 33d; ἡ. καὶ ἑταῖροι [prev. author] “Smp.” 183c, +others: with _genitive_, ἡ. τῶν λόγων 4th c.AD: Himerius Sophista “Orationes” 12.4}}:—_feminine_ **ἡλῐκι-ῶτις**, ιδος, {{Refs 1st c.AD+|1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.554a, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “DMar.” 15.2}}; ἡ. ἱστορία **contemporary** history, {{Refs 1st c.AD+|1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Pericles” 13}}; πράξεις ἡ. {{Refs 1st c.BC+|1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 1.58}}: with _dative_, **contemporaneous with**, {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|[prev. work] 9: with _genitive_, 2nd c.AD: Maximus Tyrius Sophista 3.2, 4th c.AD: Themistius Sophista “Orationes” 4.58b.}}
4916:
** συνθάπτω**,
**bury together, join in burying**, τινα {{Refs 5th c.BC+|4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 1032, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1378, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 1545, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 909c, etc.}}; τινά τινι one **with** another, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 149, 4th c.BC: Demades Orator 13, “IG” 14.943 (from Ostia)}}:—_passive_, **to be buried with**, τῷ ἀνδρί {{NT+5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.5, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.8; συνετάφη τοῖς σώμασιν ἡ ἐλευθερία 4th c.BC: Lycurgus Orator 50; συνετάφημεν [τῷ Χριστῷ] διὰ τοῦ βαπτίσματος NT.Rom.6.4.}}
4917:
** συν-θλάω**,
**crush together**, {{Refs 3rd c.BC+|3rd c.BC: Eratosthenes Epicus “Καταστερισμοί” 11, 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 2.57, 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Anabasis” 6.29.9}}:—_passive_, [ποτήριον] ὦτα συντεθλασμένον {{Refs 5th c.BC+|2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor 270, compare “IG” 22.1544.21; συνεθλάσθη τὴν κεφαλήν 5th-6th c.AD: Aeneas Gazaeus Rhetor “Theophrastus” p.32 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus; βίῃ συνθλώμενος ὀστᾶ 4th c.AD(?): Manetho Astrologus 5.201}}: _absolutely_, **to be crushed**, {{NT+4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Problemata” 863b13, NT.Matt.21.44, “Geoponica” 9.29.}}
4918:
** συνθλίβω** [ῑ],
**press together, compress**, {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1361b17, “Cael.” 307b12, 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Igne” 58, 74}}; of a crowd, {{NT|NT.Mark.5.24}}:—_passive_, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 92a, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 555b26; σ. εἰς τὴν κοιλίαν [prev. author] “Pr.” 895b2; πρὸς ἄλληλα [prev. work] 929a15}}; συντεθλιμμένον ἤτοι συνεπτυγμένον ἄργυρον, = **collisum argentum,** {{Refs|“Corpus Glossariorum Latinorum”:}}_aorist 2_ συνεθλίβην [ῐ] {{Refs 1st c.AD+|1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.408e,430c.}}
4919:

**break in pieces: crush**, τὴν καρδίαν {{NT|NT.Act.21.13.}}

4944:

4946:
** Σῠράκουσαι** [ᾱ], αἱ,
{{Refs 5th c.BC+|“Syracuse”, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.4, 2nd c.BC: Scymnus Geographus 282, “IGRom.” 1.495 (Sicily, 1st c.AD)}}; _Ionic dialect_ **Σῠρήκουσαι** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.154}}; _Doric dialect_ **Σῠράκοσαι** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 2.1, 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 22.8}}; also **Σῠράκοσσαι**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 6.6 (with variants), conjecture in 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 5.184}} (Συράκουσσ- Papyrus, as also {{Refs|“Marm.Par.” 52,71)}}: **Σῠράκουσα**, ἡ, {{Refs 1st c.BC+|1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 13.75, 14.14, 5th c.AD(?): Stephanus Byzantius}}, **Συράκουσσα** Hdn.Gr.{{Refs 4th c.AD+|1.270 codices 4th c.AD(?): Arcadius Grammaticus}}; **Σῠράκοσα**, {{Refs 1st c.BC+|1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 21.4}}; also **Σῠρακώ**, οῦς, ἡ, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 185 (name of a marsh, 5th c.AD(?): Stephanus Byzantius; called “Tyraco”, Vibius Sequester p.154 Riese)}}.-- _adjective_ **Σῠρᾱκόσιος**, α, ον, “Syracusan”, and as _substantive_ **a Syracusan, BMus.Cat.Coins Sicily** {{Refs 3rd c.BC+|p.145, Th.[same place], “IG” 12(9).1187.15 (Euboea, 3rd c.BC), etc.}}; _Ionic dialect_ and _poetry_ **Σῠρηκόσιος** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.154, “Anthologia Graeca” 5.191 (1st c.BC: Meleager Epigrammaticus), 4th-5th c.AD(?): Nonnus Epicus “Dionysiaca” 6.354}}; a form **Σῠρακόσσιος** {{Refs|Hdn.Gr. 1.120}}; **Σῠρακούσιος** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Epistulae” 326b (assuming variant)}}; **Συρρακούσιος** variant in {{Refs 4th c.AD+|4th c.AD: Libanius Sophista “Orationes” 12.36, compare 4th-5th c.AD: Choeroboscus Grammaticus “Scholia in Theodosii Canones” 2.242, +others}}; _feminine_ **Σῠρᾰκοσσίς**, γλῶσσα {{Refs 4th c.AD+|4th-5th c.AD(?): Nonnus Epicus “Dionysiaca” 9.22:}} —ἡ Συρακοσία [χώρα] **the territory of S.**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.52 (and so L. Dind. reads for ἡ Συράκουσα or Συράκοσα in 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus (see. above)): Συρακοσίων τράπεζα}}, proverbial of luxurious living, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Fragmenta” 216}}:—**Σῠρᾱκοσεύς**, έως, ὁ, {{Refs 5th c.AD+|5th c.AD(?): Stephanus Byzantius}}
4947: (i.e. γῆ); **Syria **, {{Refs 5th c.BC|Herdotus Historicus}}, etc.: Σ. ἡ Παλαιστίνη **Palestine **, {{Refs 5th c.BC|Herdotus Historicus}}: Κοίλη Σ. the district between Libanus and Anti-libanus, {{Refs 1st c.BC|Strabo Geographus}} (Middle Liddel)
4948:
** Σύρος** [ῠ], ὁ,
**Syrian,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|Inscriptiones Graecae 12.329.18, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.91 codices (variant in 2.30, 104.159, 3.5), “Tragica Adespota” 162}}; of the Λευκόσυροι, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 638, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.6 codices, 7.72 codices (but Σύριοι of the Λ., see below)}}; frequently used as a slave's name, {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Anaxandrides Comicus 51, 4th c.BC: Eriphus Comicus 6, 3rd c.BC: Hegesippus Comicus 1.4, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 45.86, “IG” 22.2937.12, etc.}}:—_feminine_ **Σύρα**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 1146 (troch.), 4th-3rd c.BC: Philemo Comicus 125}}. --Syria was called **Σῠρία**, _Ionic dialect_ -ιη, ἡ, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.105, etc.; Σ. ἡ Παλαιστίνη [prev. author] 3.91, 4.39; Σ. Παλαιστίνη “IGRom.” 3.172.22 (Ancyra, 2nd c.AD), “OGI” 601.6 (Amastris, 2nd c.AD)}}; ἡ Φοινίκη Σ. {{Refs 1st c.BC+|1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 19.93}}; Κοίλη Σ. between Lebanon and Anti-Lebanon, see at {κοῖλο; ἡ ἄνω Σ}. (uncertain reading) {{Refs 1st c.BC+|1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 2.5.38}}.--The Syrians were also called **Σύριοι**, a name which in early times was given to the Assyrians, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.63, compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 84 (Lyric poetry), 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Syr.D.” 1}}; and to the Cappadocians or Λευκόσυροι {{Refs 5th c.BC+|(1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 12.3.5. +others), 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.72, 2.104, 3.90, 5.49}}; Σ. Καππαδόκαι (variant{Σ. καὶ} K.) {{Refs|[prev. author] 1.72; Σ. οἱ ἐν τῇ Παλαιστίνῃ [prev. author] 2.104}}.-- _adjective_ **Σύριος** [ῠ], **α**, ον, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|“Syrian”, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1312, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 144 (Lyric poetry), etc.; Σ. πόα 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 627b17}}; Σ. πύλαι (see. πύλη {{Refs|11.2)}}:—also **Σῠριᾰκός**, ή, όν, {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Causis Plantarum” 2.17.3, 1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 2.1.31, etc.}}-- _adverb_ **Σῠρίηθεν** **from Syria**, {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Dionysius Periegeta 895.}}
